text:
tasha: Hey People Ops — following the major outage last week a few SREs logged a bunch of overtime (total ~48h each). Team asks if we can convert OT into comp time (time-off-in-lieu) instead of paying overtime. Is that allowed?

devon: Good question. Policy currently defaults to payout for non-exempt roles. We can consider comp time for exempt staff, but for non-exempt US hourly folks federal law generally requires OT pay, not comp time, except in public sector.

liz: From manager POV: comp time would help reduce burnout and is what the folks prefer. Can we do a hybrid: pay OT for the legally required portion and offer extra hours as comp time (up to a cap)?

payroll-bot: payroll-bot: Payroll needs employee classification (exempt/non-exempt), country, and FTE status. For US non-exempt employees, OT pay is mandatory; we can still award additional paid time off as a separate discretionary grant, but it must be taxed and coded differently (e.g., "Discretionary Comp Time Grant").

legal: legal: Confirming US federal/state rules: private employers can't substitute comp time for OT pay for non-exempt employees. For other countries, local law varies; some allow time off in lieu if documented. We should avoid retroactive policy changes.

ops-bot: ops-bot: Logged incident overtime totals to thread: https://incidents.company/INC-2026-145 (SREs: ids 88121, 88122, 88123).

tasha: Thanks. Most impacted are two non-exempt engineers and one exempt lead. Manager proposes: pay legally required OT for non-exempt hours, then grant up to 16h discretionary comp time per person to be used within 90 days. For the exempt lead, convert up to 32h into comp time. Thoughts?

devon: That approach seems reasonable operationally. Need Finance to sign off on GL mapping for the discretionary grants and confirm payroll coding. Also confirm whether the discretionary grant counts toward the 40h carryover cap.

liz: Prefer the discretionary grant not to count against annual carryover cap — we don't want to penalize folks who worked an incident. But understand auditing/usability tradeoffs.

legal: Legal advises: treat discretionary grants as taxable compensation when paid (or as PTO balance when added). If added to PTO balance, they become subject to carryover/payout policy unless we flag them in the system as "incident grant - non-carryover" with an expiry. We can implement a use-by date (e.g., 90 days) and mark no-payout on termination. We need to carefully document manager approval and the business justification.

payroll-bot: payroll-bot: For payroll ingestion, we need CSV with fields: employee_id,action,hours,effective_date,expiry_date,pay_code,no_payout,notes. Example for mixed approach:```
employee_id,action,hours,effective_date,expiry_date,pay_code,no_payout,notes
88121,pay_ot,12,2026-05-03,NA,OT,TRUE,paid overtime for incident
88122,pay_ot,12,2026-05-03,NA,OT,TRUE,paid overtime for incident
88123,grant,24,2026-05-04,2026-08-01,INC_GRT,TRUE,incident discretionary comp time grant
```

tasha: Good. So action items: 1) People Ops draft formal incident-comp guideline (how many hours eligible, caps, expiry, approval flow), 2) Payroll to confirm CSV and GL codes, 3) Legal to sign off wording for "no-payout on termination" and cross-border variation, 4) Managers to collect sign-offs from employees accepting comp time vs cash.

devon: I'll ask Finance for GL codes and confirm whether grants can be flagged as non-carryover in HRIS. Also can create a short acceptance checkbox form for employees (comp time vs cash).

legal: I'll draft standard language for the acceptance form and an internal memo outlining jurisdiction constraints (US vs UK vs AU).

liz: One more operational ask: for the exempt lead who takes comp time during a blackout week (e.g., end-of-quarter), managers must confirm coverage. We'll require manager approval each time comp time is booked.

tasha: Agreed. We'll add "manager_approval_required" and "coverage_plan" fields to the admin workflow. Also recommend limiting comp time grants that can exceed 40h to Executive approval.

ops-bot: ops-bot: Created tracker issue: /trackers/hr/INC-comp-grants-2070123456. Assigned to @devon and @tasha.

payroll-bot: payroll-bot: Payroll cutoff reminder: to affect next pay period, upload CSV before 2026-05-10 17:00 PT. If after, changes apply subsequent cycle.

tasha: Thanks all — I'll draft the guideline and post in /docs/hr/incident-comp-guideline-draft.md for review by EOD tomorrow. If Legal/Payroll want an earlier sync, ping me. :white_check_mark:
